### Subject: Opinion on ESOP perquisite taxation timing and deferred TDS for an eligible start-up

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Bluepeak Software Private Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. ## 2. Statement of Facts

Bluepeak Software Private Limited, a DPIIT-recognised eligible start-up, allotted shares to 40 employees during the year upon exercise of stock options and wishes to defer its TDS obligation as permitted for eligible start-ups.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

At what point is the ESOP perquisite taxable, how is fair market value determined, and can Bluepeak defer the related TDS deposit under Section 192(1C)?

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 17(2)(vi)
- Rule 3(8) / 3(9)
- Section 192(1C)


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CBDT Circular No. 18/2020 (ESOP deferral FAQs)

## 6. Analysis

The perquisite value, being the fair market value of the shares on the date of exercise (determined per Rule 3(8) by a registered merchant banker for unlisted companies) less the exercise price, is includible in the employee's salary income in the year of exercise. As Bluepeak qualifies as an eligible start-up, it may defer the deposit of TDS (not the taxable event itself) to the earliest of: 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, sale of the shares by the employee, or cessation of employment.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

Bluepeak may defer deposit of TDS on the ESOP perquisite under Section 192(1C) to the earliest trigger event, while the perquisite itself remains taxable in the employee's hands in the year of exercise, valued per Rule 3(8).

**Confidence level:** High
